title: AI Knowledge Assistant Platform
tagline: Enterprise AI assistant using a reusable RAG framework
summary: An enterprise AI assistant that answers questions over domain-specific company knowledge, built on a reusable RAG framework with role-based access to what each user may retrieve. I built across the stack and AWS, then moved into leading the module: client calls, guiding the developer who took over day-to-day coding, and shaping the architecture of a new document-review product.
overview: An enterprise-grade AI knowledge assistant that lets employees query internal, domain-specific knowledge and get context-aware answers generated by LLMs. At its core is a reusable Retrieval-Augmented Generation framework, so new knowledge bases can be plugged in without rebuilding the pipeline, and access control is enforced at retrieval time.

I led the module and was largely its only senior developer. In the first phase I worked hands-on across the full stack and AWS: I built the reusable RAG framework, with a junior developer I led helping out while I was busy on other work, and handled IAM roles and permissions, Secrets Manager, logging and monitoring, authorization and SSO, S3 file upload into knowledge bases, and knowledge-base use cases end to end. As the junior developer took over day-to-day coding, I moved to client calls, guiding and reviewing their work, and finalizing the architecture and data model of a new product that reviews documents against a reference document using multi-agent review generation.

points: Built the reusable RAG framework, leading a junior developer who helped while I was on other work, and delivered knowledge-base use cases on it end to end.
Built S3-backed file upload for knowledge bases, and dynamic knowledge-base selection so users can scope a conversation to the right source.
Contributed to authorization and Role-Based Access Control so users retrieve only the knowledge they are authorized to read.
Worked on SSO integration for enterprise sign-in.
Configured IAM roles and permissions and moved credentials into AWS Secrets Manager.
Set up logging and monitoring for the platform’s services.
Designed conversation history and context management for multi-turn interactions, continuity and auditability.
Added user feedback and analytics to measure and improve response quality.
Finalized the architecture and database model for a new product that reviews documents against a reference document.
Designed multi-agent review generation together with the AI developer.
Run the client calls: requirements, priorities and delivery updates.
Led and mentored the junior developer on the project, who now handles day-to-day development, and review their code.

achievements: Led the module on my own, from hands-on full-stack and AWS work to the client relationship.
Set the architecture and data model for a multi-agent document-review product.
Permission-aware retrieval: answers never leak unauthorized content.
